entries.text: Alex Rivera, product designer at a four-person studio. Fictional demo user. Splits the week between client work and a side project: a tiny habit-tracking app.
Works best in two long morning blocks; afternoons are for calls and small tasks.
Clarity over cleverness. If it needs a tooltip, it is not finished.
Quality first, then learning, then cost, then speed.
If a decision is reversible, take it in under five minutes and write down the date to review it.
Never add a feature to the side project the week a client deadline lands.
Free tools until the paid plan saves more than two hours a month.
Tool budget is about forty a month total; anything above that needs a client to pay for it.
Situation: a client asked for a dashboard redesign in two weeks. Call: shipped a one-page version first, iterated weekly. Why: a rough thing in use beats a polished thing in review.
Situation: a friend offered a paid weekend gig during a planned family trip. Call: declined. Why: trips are the one thing that does not move.
